shareSettings.intro: Path names are friendly aliases for the public links you share, so the URL reads like a word you picked instead of a random token.
shareSettings.howItWorks1: Every share link needs a public URL. Without a path name it uses a random token — unique and unguessable, but not memorable: /public/8f3ac1e2/report.pdf.
shareSettings.howItWorks2: A path name replaces that token with a word of your choice: /public/acme/report.pdf. It only changes the address — visitors still see exactly what you shared, nothing more.
shareSettings.howItWorks3: A path name is yours, not tied to a single link. Create one and reuse it for every file or folder you share from now on, so all your links follow the same pattern.
shareSettings.howItWorks4: Rename a path name and every link already published under it updates automatically — you never have to reshare anything.
shareSettings.howItWorks5: Names are reserved across the whole server, first come first served, since they appear directly in the public URL.
